title: YouTube removes its Subscriptions tab, and Figma says most big customers now use its agent weekly
dek: YouTube's new navigation, Figma's AI usage numbers, Apple's cancellation-flow messages, lessons from Lovable and Discord, a weekend watchlist, an inspiration shelf, a design power-up and three events.
preheader: YouTube moves Subscriptions out of the tab bar. Plus Figma's agent numbers and a weekend watchlist.
hero_alt: A pixel bicycle on a seaside path at sunset
summary: YouTube's biggest navigation change in about a decade is reaching phones: the [Subscriptions tab is gone from the bottom bar](https://9to5google.com/2026/11/05/youtube-app-redesign-subscriptions-tab/), now a swipe away inside Home, and early reaction is harsh, a reminder of what it costs to move a habit people rely on. Figma's third-quarter results put numbers on AI in design work: [65% of customers paying over $10K a year use the Figma agent weekly](https://www.stocktitan.net/news/FIG/figma-announces-third-quarter-2026-financial-xwr5ldww6g5v.html), and MCP use tripled in a quarter. Apple now lets apps [show a retention message inside the App Store cancellation flow](https://developer.apple.com/news/?id=fk9ps3gv), which puts a new screen, and a new ethical line, in front of subscription designers. And two teams share what they learned building: Lovable on [why it pulled autonomy back from its agent](https://lovable.dev/blog/how-we-built-lovable-and-why-we-keep-rebuilding-it), Discord on the [small craft rules behind its new video player](https://discord.com/blog/modernizing-the-video-playback-experience-at-discord).

reads.title: YouTube's app redesign drops the Subscriptions tab
reads.note: The five-button bar gives way to one built around Shorts and creating, with Subscriptions moved to a swipe inside Home next to a custom feed; read it with the user reaction as a live case of platform goals overriding a well-worn habit.

reads.title: Figma's third quarter: two in three big customers use its agent every week
reads.note: Revenue rose 43% to $391.4M, over 80% of customers paying $10K or more used AI credits, MCP use tripled and writing back into files grew fourfold, and Dylan Field argues value is moving up the stack to design.

reads.title: Apple adds retention messages to the subscription cancellation flow
reads.note: Apps can now show text, images or a special offer when someone cancels, set who sees it and how often in App Store Connect, and pick a message per subscriber through a new API; worth deciding now where persuasion ends and obstruction starts.

reads.title: How we built Lovable, and why we keep rebuilding it
reads.note: Co-founder Anton Osika explains why fully autonomous agents wandered off, why they went back to a step-by-step flow people can review, and why short notes on recurring mistakes beat fine-tuning, lessons that apply to any AI feature you design.

reads.title: Modernizing the video playback experience at Discord
reads.note: One player replaced four, with craft rules worth copying: no tap target under 24px from a small tile to fullscreen, tabular figures so the time doesn't jitter, its own clock for a smooth playhead, and tests written before the refactor.

watch.title: How to stand out in a world of AI designs
watch.note: A 48-minute YC session on how designers and products stand apart once anyone can generate a polished interface, the question sitting under this week's Figma agent numbers. The long watch for the weekend.

watch.title: Kyle Barber: designing Inflight (the raw behind-the-scenes)
watch.note: An hour behind the scenes with Kyle Barber on how Inflight was designed, the kind of process walkthrough that shows the decisions a finished case study usually leaves out.

watch.title: Explore shaders and motion with the Figma agent
watch.note: A five-minute official walkthrough of asking the Figma agent for shaders and motion, timely now that Figma says two in three of its biggest customers use the agent every week.

watch.title: An 86-minute guide to finding product-market fit
watch.note: Rob Snyder, author of The Power of Pull, on how teams find product-market fit, useful context for designers whose work now often starts before a product is proven.

watch.title: Config India 2026: the work has to leave the file
watch.note: Ashish Kashyap and Saptarshi Prakash at Config India on getting design work out of the file and into the product, a 20-minute talk from the Indian design community that went up last week.

learn.title: Impeccable gives your coding agent a design vocabulary and a check for AI-looking UI
learn.intro: Paul Bakaus's open-source skill, which grew out of Anthropic's frontend-design skill, adds 24 design commands to coding agents such as Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and Copilot. Version 4.8.0 arrived on 26 October, a week after 4.7.0 added two new typography checks, so it is a good moment to try it on a real screen.
changes: You steer with design words instead of long prompts: bolder, quieter, distill, typeset, layout, animate and more, plus polish, harden and adapt for the finishing pass.
Critique gives a scored UX review and audit ranks accessibility, performance, theming and responsive issues from P0 to P3.
Init writes a PRODUCT.md and document writes a DESIGN.md, so the agent keeps to your product and brand across sessions.
A detector with 62 fixed rules, no AI or API key needed, flags tells such as Inter everywhere, purple-to-blue gradients, cards inside cards and grey text on colour.

install.where: Any supported agent, in your project's terminal
install.how: Run the installer; it finds the AI tools you use and asks whether to install for this project or globally. Run update later to get new versions.
Add the marketplace, then open /plugin and install Impeccable from there.

learn.try: Run /impeccable init once for the project, then ask: /impeccable critique the pricing cards.
learn.take: The commands are most useful once init has written PRODUCT.md, so spend five minutes on that first. Treat the detector's list as a review prompt rather than a verdict; some rules, like contrast, only run when it scans a live URL.
